## 3. Narrative Analysis

### Recurring Cross-Language Constructional Patterns

**Predicative attribution (Function A) is the most universal construction type in the dataset.** All eight languages use a subject + copula/predicate construction to assert that something is true, false, genuine, accurate, valid, or honest. The main variation is in the form of the copula: Georgian uses an enclitic *-a* as the default (with the full copula *aris* required under negation), Yoruba uses a zero copula for stative predicates but requires *jẹ́* for nominal predicates, Finnish requires the partitive *totta* in the specific *olla totta* construction, Basque uses the 3sg copula *da* throughout, Tamil uses a zero copula with optional emphatic particles, Indonesian uses a zero copula with *adalah/merupakan* available in formal registers, Turkish uses a null copula as default with the *-dır* suffix restricted to formal/assertive contexts, and Korean uses *-ida* as the standard copular suffix. Despite this surface variation, the underlying constructional function is identical across all eight languages.

**The intransitive truth-revelation construction (Function J, intransitive) is documented in all eight languages and shows a consistent structural pattern.** In every language, truth can be the grammatical subject of an intransitive verb expressing emergence or disclosure. The spatial metaphor of truth "coming to light" or "coming to the surface" is consistent across all eight languages and all language families represented. This is one of the most robust cross-linguistic constructional patterns in the dataset. The specific verb varies (Georgian *gamovida*, Yoruba *farahàn*, Finnish *tulee ilmi*, Basque *ateratzen da azalera*, Tamil *veḷippaṭṭatu*, Indonesian *terungkap*, Turkish *ortaya çıktı*, Korean *드러나다/밝혀지다*), but the constructional pattern — truth as subject, intransitive emergence verb as predicate — is consistent.

**The agentive asymmetry (Function G) is consistent across all eight languages.** Every language has lexicalized single-word agentives for habitual liars and forgers, but none has a parallel lexicalized agentive for habitual truth-tellers. This is explicitly documented in the F4 construction tables for all eight languages and is not a gap in documentation. The concept of "truth-teller" is expressed periphrastically in all eight languages. This asymmetry is consistent across unrelated language families (South Caucasian, Niger-Congo, Finno-Ugric, isolate, Dravidian, Austronesian, Turkic, Koreanic) and appears to reflect a cross-linguistic pattern in how the truth domain is lexicalized.

**The discourse-framing construction (Function H) is present in all eight languages but shows the widest variation in degree of grammaticalization.** At one extreme, Indonesian *sebenarnya* and Turkish *aslında* are fully grammaticalized discourse markers whose compositional meanings are no longer active. At the other extreme, Yoruba uses a hortative construction (*jẹ́ kí a sọ òtítọ́*, let us speak the truth) for the same discourse function rather than a grammaticalized adverbial. Between these extremes, Georgian *simartle rom vtq̇vat* is a subjunctive construction that retains compositional transparency, Finnish *totta puhuen* is a participial phrase, Basque *egia esan behar* is a purposive construction, Tamil *uṇmaiyil* is a locative case form, and Korean *사실을 말하자면* is a conditional verbal phrase. The functional outcome is the same across all eight languages — signaling that what follows is the speaker's honest assessment or a correction of a prior assumption — but the constructional form varies from fully grammaticalized to fully compositional.

**The abstract nominalization strategy (Function F) is universal and productive in all eight languages.** Every language produces abstract nouns naming truth-domain qualities through a suffix or circumfix on an adjectival or verbal base. The specific morphological mechanism varies — Turkish *-luk*, Finnish *-uus*, Basque *-tasun*, Tamil *-mai*, Indonesian *ke-...-an* circumfix, Korean *-seong*, Georgian *-eba/-oba*, Yoruba *ì-* prefix — but the functional outcome is the same. In all languages, the resulting nominal names the property as an abstract entity and participates in evaluative constructions. This pattern is productive in all eight languages and shows no signs of fossilization.

**The proverbial assertion that truth ultimately prevails (Function J, proverbial) is documented in all eight languages.** Georgian *simartle gamarjvebs* (truth prevails), Yoruba *òtítọ́ kò ní kú* (truth will not die), Finnish *totuus tulee ilmi* (used in this proverbial sense), Basque *egia beti ateratzen da azalera* (the truth always comes to the surface), Tamil *uṇmai tāṉ vellum* (truth alone will prevail), Indonesian *kebenaran akan terungkap pada akhirnya* (the truth will come out in the end), Turkish *gerçek er ya da geç ortaya çıkar* (the truth comes out sooner or later), Korean *진실은 하나다* (there is only one truth). The specific framing varies, but the proverbial register is present in all eight languages.

---

### Important Asymmetries, Substitutions, and Restrictions

**The most important asymmetry is the one-way blocked pathway for truth-teller agentives.** As documented above, all eight languages have lexicalized agentives for liars and forgers but none for truth-tellers. This is not a gap in documentation; it is explicitly noted in the F4 construction tables for all eight languages. The asymmetry is consistent across unrelated language families.

**The *있다/없다* existential frame in Korean substitutes for the copular predication strategy used in other languages for abstract quality nominals.** In Korean, *-seong* quality nominals (*진정성*, *신빙성*, *타당성*) cannot take *-hada* as a predicative suffix; they require the existential *있다/없다* frame instead. This is a morphological restriction documented in the F4 construction tables for Korean and has no parallel in other languages. In all other languages, abstract quality nominals participate in the standard copular predication construction (Function A). The Korean restriction creates a constructional substitution: where other languages say "it is credible" (copular predication), Korean says "credibility exists" (existential predication).

**The *osoittautua* + translative construction in Finnish substitutes for the periphrastic *menjadi/di* constructions used in other languages for inchoative truth-evaluation.** Finnish uses the verb *osoittautua* (to turn out to be) with a translative case complement (*väite osoittautui epätodeksi*, the claim turned out to be false) as the primary inchoative construction for truth-domain adjectives. The translative case is obligatory and encodes the resultant state. Other languages use periphrastic constructions with general-purpose change-of-state verbs (Indonesian *menjadi*, Basque *bihurtu*, Turkish *çıkmak*, Korean *밝혀지다/드러나다*) without a dedicated case form for the resultant state.

**The *fi* instrumental serial verb construction in Yoruba substitutes for the morphological causative constructions used in other languages.** Yoruba uses the serial verb *fi* (use/take) as the primary causative strategy: *ó fi ẹ̀rí hàn lójú ìgbìmọ̀* (he presented evidence before the court), *wọ́n fi ìtànjẹ́ gbà owó rẹ̀* (they used deception to take his money). This construction encodes the instrument or means by which an outcome is brought about. Other languages use morphological causatives (Finnish *väärentää*, Turkish *doğrulamak*, Indonesian *memalsukan*) or transitive verbs (Georgian *gaq̇alba*, Korean *위조하다*) for the same function.

**The *değil* negation strategy in Turkish is more restricted than the negation strategies in other languages.** In Turkish, *değil* is the sole negation strategy for adjectival predicates; no alternate negation construction is attested in this domain. In other languages, multiple negation strategies are available: Georgian has both *ar aris* (syntactic) and *u-...-o* privative circumfix (morphological); Finnish has both *ei ole* (syntactic) and *epä-* prefix (morphological); Indonesian has both *tidak* (syntactic, for adjectival predicates) and *bukan* (syntactic, for nominal predicates); Korean has both *아니다* (for nominal predicates) and *-지 않다* (for adjectival predicates).

**The *bukan/tidak* distinction in Indonesian and the *아니다/-지 않다* distinction in Korean represent a cross-linguistically unusual split in negation strategy based on predicate type.** In both languages, nominal predicates and adjectival predicates require different negation forms: Indonesian *bukan* (nominal) vs. *tidak* (adjectival), Korean *아니다* (nominal) vs. *-지 않다* (adjectival). This split is not documented in the other six languages, where a single negation strategy applies across both predicate types.

**The post-nominal modifier position in Yoruba is the reverse of all other languages in the dataset.** In Yoruba, truth-domain evaluative modifiers follow the head noun (*ènìyàn òtítọ́*, a truthful person; *ẹ̀rí ojú*, eyewitness evidence), while in all other seven languages the modifier precedes the head noun. This is not a minor variation but a systematic structural difference in the direction of modification.

**The three-way inchoative verb distinction in Korean (*드러나다/밝혀지다/판명되다*) substitutes for the single inchoative verb used in most other languages.** Korean documents three distinct inchoative verbs for truth-revelation with slightly different nuances: *드러나다* (exposed/surfaced, stronger sense of unwanted revelation), *밝혀지다* (revealed through investigation, more neutral), *판명되다* (officially determined, most formal). Other languages typically use a single inchoative verb for this function. The Korean three-way distinction encodes nuances of agency, formality, and the nature of the revelation process that other languages express through context or additional modifiers.

---

### Cases Where a Function Is Weakly Expressed, Constructionally Indirect, or Absent

**The discourse-framing function (Function H) is most weakly expressed in Yoruba.** While all other languages have a grammaticalized or semi-grammaticalized adverbial form for introducing frank disclosures or corrections, Yoruba uses a hortative construction (*jẹ́ kí a sọ òtítọ́*, let us speak the truth) for this function. This construction is more compositionally transparent and less grammaticalized than the equivalents in other languages. The F4 data for Yoruba does not document a grammaticalized discourse marker parallel to Indonesian *sebenarnya*, Turkish *aslında*, or Tamil *uṇmaiyil*.

**The existential/scalar predication function (Function I) is most weakly expressed in Georgian, Finnish, and Turkish.** In these languages, abstract quality nominals participate in the standard copular predication construction (Function A) rather than in a dedicated existential or scalar frame. The *있다/없다* existential frame documented in Korean, and the *badago/ez dago* frame documented in Basque, have no parallel in Georgian, Finnish, or Turkish. In these languages, the evaluative question "does this source have credibility?" is expressed through the same copular construction as "is this statement true?" — there is no constructional differentiation between the two evaluative targets.

**The morphological causative-inchoative chain (Function E, morphological chain) is absent or marginal in Yoruba, Tamil, and Korean.** While Turkish shows a productive *-laş-/-leş-tir-* chain and Basque shows a *-tu* causative on adjectival bases, Yoruba, Tamil, and Korean do not document this chain. In these languages, causative meaning is expressed through light-verb constructions (Yoruba *fi...hàn*, Tamil *col/pēcu*, Korean *하다*) rather than through morphological causative derivation.

**The morphological inchoative (Function D, morphological) is restricted or absent in most languages.** Only Georgian (*-deba* suffix, restricted to the *mart-* root), Turkish (*-laş/-leş* suffix, restricted to some bases), and Basque (*-tu* intransitive, lexically restricted) show morphological inchoatives in the truth domain. In Finnish, the morphological inchoative (*aitoutua*, to become authentic) is explicitly marked as marginal. In Yoruba, Tamil, Indonesian, and Korean, the periphrastic inchoative (Function D, periphrastic) is the only documented strategy. The morphological inchoative is thus a minority strategy in the dataset, with the periphrastic inchoative being the universal default.

**The parallel morphological opposition for verification/falsification (documented in Turkish as *doğrulamak/yanlışlamak*) is absent in most languages.** While Turkish shows a productive morphological pair encoding the verification/falsification distinction with parallel derivational stacking (*doğrulanabilirlik/yanlışlanabilirlik*), no other language in the dataset shows this as a productive morphological pair. Finnish has *todistaa* (to prove) and *osoittaa epätodeksi* (to show to be false), but these are not morphologically parallel. Basque has *frogatu* (to prove) and *gezurtatu* (to give the lie to), but these are not a parallel pair encoding the same philosophical distinction. This is a single-language observation for Turkish.

**The three-way verifiability distinction (*egiaztagarria/egiaztagaitza/egiaztaezina*) documented in Basque is absent in all other languages.** No other language in the dataset documents a three-way morphological distinction within the verifiability sub-domain. Other languages show only a binary verifiable/unverifiable opposition. The Basque three-way distinction — capable of being verified / difficult to verify / impossible to verify — is a single-language observation.

**The *-hada/-doeda* stative/agentive distinction documented in Korean is absent in all other languages.** Korean documents a systematic semantic distinction between *jinsil-hada* (to be truthful, active/performed quality) and *jinsil-doeda* (to be truthful, inherent/resultant quality). This morphological distinction between performed and inherent quality is not documented in any other language in the dataset. In all other languages, a single predicative form covers both the active/performed and the inherent/resultant readings of truth-domain predicates.

**The concessive construction (Function H, concessive) is not documented in Yoruba in the F4 data.** While all other seven languages show a documented construction for acknowledging a truth claim while introducing a qualification, the F4 data for Yoruba does not include this pattern. This may reflect a gap in documentation rather than a genuine absence, but it cannot be confirmed from the available data.

## Preliminary Notes on Methodology

The dimensions and constructional functions below are named from patterns documented in the F-phase and prior G-phase data. No external theoretical framework is applied. Where the data shows a dimension split, merged, or only partially recoverable across languages, this is noted explicitly. The matrix cells record cross-language evidence as ALLOWED, BLOCKED, VARIABLE, or INSUFFICIENT DATA, with brief supporting notes. The narrative analysis follows the matrix.

## Semantic Dimensions (from data)

The following twelve dimensions are derived from the G3 axis comparison and confirmed by F3 semantic grouping tables across languages. They are listed here with brief reminders of their empirical basis.

**D1: Propositional Correspondence** — Whether a specific statement or claim matches what is actually the case. Evaluative target: a proposition or utterance. Attested in all 8 languages.

**D2: Personal Honesty and Integrity in Conduct** — Whether a person's habitual conduct and character are free from deception. Evaluative target: a person or their pattern of behavior. Attested in all 8 languages.

**D3: Source Trustworthiness vs. Content Credibility** — Whether a source can be depended upon (source evaluation) vs. whether a specific claim merits belief (content evaluation). Attested in all 8 languages; the source/content sub-distinction is explicitly documented in at least 4 languages.

**D4: Genuineness of Objects vs. Fraudulent Imitation** — Whether a physical item, document, or credential is what it purports to be vs. a fraudulent substitute. Evaluative target: a physical item. Attested in all 8 languages; neutral-copy vs. fraudulent-fake sub-distinction in at least 6.

**D5: Legal/Procedural Validity vs. Moral/Substantive Legitimacy** — Whether an action or document meets formal legal conditions (validity) vs. whether it is rightful in a broader normative sense (legitimacy). Attested in all 8 languages.

**D6: Precision and Exactness of Correspondence** — The degree to which a measurement, description, or representation corresponds closely and exactly to its referent. Scalar rather than binary. Clearly lexicalized in at least 6 languages; less elaborated in yo and ta as a distinct dimension.

**D7: Authenticity of Inner States and Expressed Feelings** — Whether a person's expressed feelings, intentions, or commitments reflect genuine inner conviction rather than performance or pretense. Attested in all 8 languages; degree of elaboration varies considerably.

**D8: Appearance vs. Underlying Reality** — The contrast between how something appears on the surface and what it actually is. Attested in at least 6 languages with explicit documentation; less elaborated in yo and ta.

**D9: Evidential Grounding and Proof** — Whether a claim is supported by adequate evidence, and the processes by which evidence is produced and used to establish truth. Attested in all 8 languages.

**D10: Truth Revelation and Concealment as Processes** — The dynamics by which truth is brought to light, concealed, sought, or suppressed. Treats truth as an entity that can emerge or be hidden. Attested in all 8 languages.

**D11: Correctness of Reasoning, Judgment, and Understanding** — Whether a judgment, inference, or interpretation follows properly from evidence or reasoning. Evaluative target: a cognitive process or its output. Attested in all 8 languages; degree of differentiation from D1 varies.

**D12: Deliberate Deception vs. Innocent Error** — The distinction between falsehoods produced with intent to deceive and those produced through honest mistake or misunderstanding. Attested in all 8 languages; explicitly documented in F3 grouping tables for at least 6.

---

## Constructional Functions (from data)

The following constructional functions are derived from the F4 construction tables and G5 construction comparison. They represent the main realization types documented across languages.

**CF1: Predicative Attribution** — Subject + copula/predicate construction asserting a truth-domain property of a subject. Includes both nominal predicates (it is a lie) and adjectival predicates (it is correct). Attested in all 8 languages.

**CF2: Negative Attribution** — Syntactic or morphological negation of a truth-domain predicate. Includes syntactic negation (not true), morphological privative (unreliable), and double negation. Attested in all 8 languages.

**CF3: Adnominal Modification** — A truth-domain evaluative term modifies a noun (accurate information, forged document, reliable source). Attested in all 8 languages.

**CF4: Inchoative / Change-of-State** — A subject transitions into a truth-domain state (the truth comes to light, the claim turned out to be false, the contract became void). Includes periphrastic and morphological inchoatives. Attested in all 8 languages.

**CF5: Causative** — An agent causes a truth-domain state (to forge a document, to verify information, to reveal the truth, to conceal the truth). Includes morphological causatives, light-verb causatives, and serial verb causatives. Attested in all 8 languages.

**CF6: Abstract Nominalization** — A suffix or circumfix produces an abstract noun naming a truth-domain quality as an entity (truthfulness, accuracy, credibility, validity). Attested in all 8 languages.

**CF7: Agentive Nominalization** — A morphological process produces a nominal denoting a habitual agent of a truth-domain action (liar, forger, deceiver). Attested in all 8 languages for negative roles; absent for positive roles (truth-teller) in all 8 languages.

**CF8: Discourse Framing** — A grammaticalized or semi-grammaticalized expression functions as a sentence-level marker signaling frank disclosure, correction of a prior assumption, or truth-asserting stance. Attested in all 8 languages; degree of grammaticalization varies.

**CF9: Existential / Scalar Predication** — An abstract quality nominal combines with an existential verb (have/exist) or scalar predicate (high/low) to evaluate whether a quality is present or to what degree. Attested in at least 5 languages; most systematically documented in ko.

**CF10: Truth-Revelation / Concealment Construction** — Truth is the grammatical subject of an intransitive emergence or concealment verb (the truth came out, the truth was revealed). Attested in all 8 languages.

**CF11: Parallel Morphological Opposition** — The same derivational process applies to both a truth base and a falsity base, producing a morphologically parallel pair of opposing forms (verify/falsify, verifiable/falsifiable). Attested as a fully productive pattern only in tr; partial parallels in fi and eu.

**CF12: Proverbial / Fixed Moral Assertion** — A fixed or semi-fixed construction asserts a moral or epistemic claim about truth (truth will prevail, a lie has short legs, truth is bitter). Attested in all 8 languages.

### D9 (Evidential Grounding and Proof)

**CF4 (Inchoative / Change-of-State) — VARIABLE:** Inchoative constructions for a claim becoming proven or evidence emerging are attested in some languages (fi *väite tuli todistetuksi*, the claim came to be proven; ko *사실로 밝혀지다*, to be revealed as fact; id *terbukti*, to be proven) but the pattern is not as consistently documented as for D1.

**CF7 (Agentive Nominalization) — VARIABLE:** Agentive nominals for witnesses, judges, and examiners are attested in several languages (yo *ẹlẹ́rìí*, witness; fi *todistaja*, witness; ko *증인*, witness; eu *lekukoa*, witness) but these are institutional role nouns rather than agentive nominals derived from the proof/evidence bases themselves.

**CF10 (Truth-Revelation / Concealment) — VARIABLE:** The truth-revelation construction overlaps with D9 in some languages (fi *totuus tulee ilmi* can describe the emergence of evidence; ko *진실이 밝혀지다* can describe the establishment of a fact through evidence) but the construction is primarily associated with D1 and D10 rather than D9.

**CF11 (Parallel Morphological Opposition) — VARIABLE:** The tr *doğrulamak/yanlışlamak* pair (verify/falsify) and the eu *egiaztagarria/egiaztaezina* pair (verifiable/unverifiable) are the most explicitly documented parallel morphological oppositions for D9. These are attested in 2–3 languages rather than broadly across all 8.

**CF12 (Proverbial / Fixed Moral Assertion) — VARIABLE:** Some proverbial expressions about evidence and proof are attested (yo *ẹ̀rí ojú* as the most reliable evidence type; ka *utyuari mtkicebuleba*, irrefutable evidence) but the proverbial pattern is less consistently documented for D9 than for D1.

### D10 (Truth Revelation and Concealment as Processes)

**CF1 (Predicative Attribution) — VARIABLE:** Standard predicative attribution (the truth is X) is less characteristic of D10 than of D1. D10 is primarily expressed through CF4 (inchoative), CF5 (causative), and CF10 (truth-revelation construction) rather than through static predication.

**CF2 (Negative Attribution) — VARIABLE:** Negation of truth-revelation constructions is attested (ko *진실이 드러나지 않았다*, the truth did not emerge; fi *totuus ei tullut ilmi*, the truth did not come to light) but is less characteristic of D10 than of D1.

**CF3 (Adnominal Modification) — VARIABLE:** Adnominal modification is attested for D10 nominals (ka *simarṭlis gamovlena*, revelation of truth; ko *진실 규명*, truth investigation) but is less characteristic of D10 than of D1 or D4.

**CF8 (Discourse Framing) — VARIABLE:** Some languages document discourse frames associated with D10 (ko *사실을 말하자면*, to tell the truth; fi *totta puhuen*, to tell the truth) but these are primarily associated with D1 (frank disclosure of a proposition) rather than D10 (the process of truth emerging from concealment).

**CF9 (Existential / Scalar Predication) — INSUFFICIENT DATA:** The existential frame is not documented for D10 process nominals. The process of truth-revelation is expressed through CF4 and CF10 rather than through existential predication.

### D11 (Correctness of Reasoning, Judgment, and Understanding)

**CF4 (Inchoative / Change-of-State) — VARIABLE:** Inchoative constructions for a judgment becoming correct or a reasoning process being vindicated are attested in some languages (ka *gamarṭleba*, vindication; tr *haklı çıkmak*, to be proven right; ko *타당성이 인정되다*, validity is recognized) but are not as systematically documented as for D1.

**CF5 (Causative) — VARIABLE:** Causative constructions for making a judgment correct or justifying a claim are attested in some languages (ka *gamarṭleba*, justification; tr *haklı kılmak*, to justify; fi *perustella*, to justify/give reasons for) but are not as consistently documented as causatives for D4 or D9.

**CF7 (Agentive Nominalization) — VARIABLE:** Agentive nominals for judges, reasoners, and evaluators are attested in some languages (yo *adájọ́*, judge; ko *판사*, judge; fi *arvioija*, evaluator) but these are institutional role nouns rather than agentive nominals derived from the correctness-of-reasoning bases themselves.

**CF8 (Discourse Framing) — VARIABLE:** Some languages document precision-marking discourse frames that overlap with D11 (ka *martebulad*, correctly/appropriately; fi *tarkasti ottaen*, strictly speaking; ko *정확히 말하면*, to be precise) but these are not as consistently documented as the frank-disclosure frames associated with D1.

**CF9 (Existential / Scalar Predication) — VARIABLE:** The existential frame is attested for validity/soundness nominals in some languages (ko *타당성이 있다/없다*, to have/lack validity; eu *arrazoizkoa da/ez da*, it is/is not reasonable) but is not the primary predication strategy for D11 in most languages.

**CF10 (Truth-Revelation / Concealment) — INSUFFICIENT DATA:** The truth-revelation construction is not documented for D11 (correctness of reasoning) nominals. Reasoning correctness is not treated as an entity that emerges from concealment in the documented data.

### D12 (Deliberate Deception vs. Innocent Error)

**CF4 (Inchoative / Change-of-State) — VARIABLE:** Inchoative constructions for a deception being exposed or an error being corrected are attested in some languages (fi *valhe paljastui*, the lie was exposed; ko *거짓말이 들통나다*, the lie was caught out; id *kebohongannya terungkap*, his lie came to light) but are not as systematically documented as for D1.

**CF5 (Causative) — VARIABLE:** Causative constructions for causing deception or correcting an error are attested in some languages (fi *väärentää*, to forge; id *membohongi*, to deceive someone; ko *속이다*, to deceive) but the distinction between deliberate deception and innocent error is not consistently encoded in the causative construction itself.

**CF7 (Agentive Nominalization) — ALLOWED (negative: liar, deceiver) / BLOCKED (positive: truth-teller):** This is the most consistently documented asymmetry in the dataset. Negative agentive nominals for liars and deceivers are attested in all 8 languages. Positive agentive nominals for truth-tellers are absent or marginal in all 8 languages. The asymmetry is explicitly noted in the F4 construction tables for all 8 languages.

**CF9 (Existential / Scalar Predication) — INSUFFICIENT DATA:** The existential frame is not documented for D12 nominals. The distinction between deliberate deception and innocent error is expressed through lexical choice (different terms for lie vs. error) rather than through existential predication.

**CF10 (Truth-Revelation / Concealment) — VARIABLE:** The truth-revelation construction is attested for D12 in some languages (fi *valhe paljastui*, the lie was exposed; ko *거짓말이 들통나다*, the lie was caught out) but the construction treats the deception as an entity that emerges from concealment, which is structurally parallel to D1 and D10 rather than specific to D12.

## Narrative Analysis

### Strongly Recurrent Constraints

**1. Predicative attribution (CF1) is ALLOWED for all twelve semantic dimensions without documented restriction.** Every language uses a subject + copula/predicate construction to assert truth-domain properties across all dimensions. The specific copular form varies (enclitic in ka, zero copula in ta/id/tr, overt copula in fi/eu/yo/ko) but the constructional function is universally available. This is the most robust positive constraint in the dataset.

**2. Adnominal modification (CF3) is ALLOWED for all twelve semantic dimensions without documented restriction.** Every language places truth-domain evaluative terms as modifiers of nouns across all dimensions. The modifier position varies (prenominal in ka/fi/eu/ta/id/tr/ko; postnominal in yo) but the constructional function is universally available. The yo postnominal pattern is the only structural divergence, and it is consistent within yo rather than being a restriction on specific dimensions.

**3. Abstract nominalization (CF6) is ALLOWED for all twelve semantic dimensions.** Every language produces abstract nouns naming truth-domain qualities across all dimensions. The specific suffix varies but the functional outcome is consistent. This is the second most robust positive constraint in the dataset.

**4. The agentive asymmetry (CF7) is a BLOCKED pathway for positive roles across all dimensions and all languages.** No language in the dataset has a lexicalized single-word agentive nominal for a habitual truth-teller, honest person (as a role noun), or authenticator. This asymmetry is documented explicitly in the F4 construction tables for all 8 languages and is consistent across unrelated language families. The negative pole (liar, forger, deceiver, hypocrite) is ALLOWED for CF7 across D1, D2, D4, D7, and D12. The positive pole is BLOCKED for CF7 across all dimensions. This is the most consistently documented blocked pathway in the dataset.

**5. The truth-revelation / concealment construction (CF10) is ALLOWED for D1 (Propositional Correspondence) and D10 (Truth Revelation and Concealment as Processes) across all 8 languages.** The intransitive construction in which truth is the grammatical subject of an emergence verb is documented in all 8 languages for D1 and D10 nominals. The spatial metaphor of truth "coming to light" or "coming to the surface" is consistent across all language families. This is one of the most robust constructional patterns in the dataset.

**6. Proverbial / fixed moral assertion (CF12) is ALLOWED for D1 (Propositional Correspondence) across all 8 languages.** Every language documents at least one proverbial or semi-fixed construction asserting the ultimate triumph or indestructibility of truth. The specific formulation varies (truth will not die, truth will prevail, truth always comes to the surface, there is only one truth) but the proverbial register is present in all 8 languages for D1. CF12 is VARIABLE or INSUFFICIENT DATA for most other dimensions.

**7. Negative attribution (CF2) is ALLOWED for all twelve semantic dimensions.** Every language has a strategy for negating truth-domain predicates across all dimensions. The specific negation strategy varies (syntactic negation particle, morphological privative prefix, negative copula) but the constructional function is universally available.

### Likely Prohibitions or Avoidance Patterns

**1. The positive-role agentive nominalization pathway is blocked across all dimensions and all languages.** This is the most consistently documented prohibition in the dataset. The derivational process that generates liars, forgers, and deceivers does not generate truth-tellers, authenticators, or honest persons as role nouns in any of the 8 languages. The concept is expressed periphrastically in all 8 languages. This asymmetry is consistent across South Caucasian, Niger-Congo, Finno-Ugric, language isolate, Dravidian, Austronesian, Turkic, and Koreanic language families.

**2. The truth-revelation / concealment construction (CF10) is not documented for D5 (Legal/Procedural Validity), D6 (Precision and Exactness), D9 (Evidential Grounding), or D11 (Correctness of Reasoning).** The construction treats truth as an entity that moves between hidden and visible states. This framing is not applied to validity, precision, evidence, or reasoning correctness in the documented data. These dimensions are expressed through CF1 (predicative attribution), CF4 (inchoative), and CF5 (causative) rather than through the emergence-from-concealment construction. The absence is consistent across languages and appears to reflect a semantic constraint: the emergence-from-concealment framing is restricted to dimensions where truth is conceptualized as a hidden entity (D1, D10) rather than as a property of objects, processes, or reasoning.

**3. Discourse framing (CF8) is not documented for D3 (Source Trustworthiness), D4 (Genuineness of Objects), D5 (Legal/Procedural Validity), D9 (Evidential Grounding), or D12 (Deliberate Deception vs. Innocent Error).** The discourse-framing constructions documented in the data (sebenarnya, aslında, simartle rom vtq̇vat, uṇmaiyil, etc.) are associated with D1 (frank disclosure of a proposition) and to a lesser extent D8 (appearance vs. underlying reality). They are not documented as sentence-level markers for source evaluation, object authentication, legal validity, evidence assessment, or the deception/error distinction. This absence is consistent across languages.

**4. The parallel morphological opposition (CF11) is not broadly attested.** The tr *doğrulamak/yanlışlamak* pair is the only fully productive parallel morphological opposition encoding the verify/falsify distinction in the dataset. Partial parallels exist in fi and eu. The pattern is not documented in ka, yo, ta, id, or ko. This suggests that the parallel morphological encoding of opposing epistemic operations is a language-specific elaboration rather than a cross-linguistically available construction type.

**5. Proverbial / fixed moral assertion (CF12) is not documented for D6 (Precision and Exactness).** No language in the dataset documents a proverbial construction about precision or exactness. The proverbial register is associated with D1 (truth will prevail), D2 (honesty is the best policy), D10 (truth always comes to the surface), and to a lesser extent D5 (justice will prevail) and D12 (a lie has short legs). The absence of proverbial constructions for D6 is consistent across all 8 languages and appears to reflect the scalar, technical nature of precision evaluation, which does not lend itself to the moral-assertion register.

### Important Divergences, Substitutions, and Asymmetries

**1. The existential / scalar predication construction (CF9) substitutes for standard copular predication (CF1) for abstract quality nominals in Korean.** In ko, *-seong* quality nominals (*진정성*, *신빙성*, *타당성*) cannot take *-hada* as a predicative suffix; they require the existential *있다/없다* frame instead. This is a morphological restriction unique to ko in the dataset. In all other languages, abstract quality nominals participate in the standard copular predication construction (CF1). The ko restriction creates a constructional substitution: where other languages say "it is credible" (CF1), ko says "credibility exists" (CF9). This substitution is documented for D3, D7, D9, and D11 in ko.

**2. The inchoative construction (CF4) shows the widest variation in realization across languages.** The periphrastic inchoative (become X, turn out to be X) is the universal default across all dimensions and all languages. Morphological inchoatives are restricted: ka *-deba* is documented only for the *mart-* root within the truth domain; tr *-laş/-leş* is productive for some bases but not others; eu *-tu* intransitive is lexically restricted; fi *-utua* is marginal for truth-domain adjectives. The morphological inchoative is a minority strategy in the dataset, with the periphrastic inchoative being the universal default. This variation is consistent across dimensions: CF4 is ALLOWED for all dimensions but the specific realization varies considerably.

**3. The causative construction (CF5) shows a consistent asymmetry between the forgery/falsification domain and the verification/authentication domain.** Causative constructions for forging, falsifying, and deceiving are more consistently documented and more morphologically elaborated than causative constructions for verifying, authenticating, and confirming. In fi, *väärentää* (to forge) is a fully lexicalized morphological causative, while *todentaa* (to verify/authenticate) is more recent and more restricted in distribution. In id, *memalsukan* (to falsify) is a standard legal term, while *membenarkan* (to confirm) covers both epistemic confirmation and deontic permission. In ko, *위조하다* (to forge) is a standard legal term, while *진실을 밝히다* (to reveal the truth) is a light-verb construction. This asymmetry parallels the agentive asymmetry (CF7): the negative pole (forging, deceiving) is more morphologically elaborated than the positive pole (verifying, authenticating).

**4. The discourse-framing construction (CF8) shows the widest variation in degree of grammaticalization across languages.** At one extreme, id *sebenarnya* and tr *aslında* are fully grammaticalized discourse markers whose compositional meanings are no longer active. At the other extreme, yo uses a hortative construction (*jẹ́ kí a sọ òtítọ́*, let us speak the truth) for the same discourse function rather than a grammaticalized adverbial. Between these extremes, ka *simartle rom vtq̇vat* is a subjunctive construction, fi *totta puhuen* is a participial phrase, eu *egia esan behar* is a purposive construction, ta *uṇmaiyil* is a locative case form, and ko *사실을 말하자면* is a conditional verbal phrase. The functional outcome is the same across all 8 languages — signaling frank disclosure or correction of a prior assumption — but the constructional form varies from fully grammaticalized to fully compositional. This variation is consistent across D1 (the primary dimension for CF8) and does not appear to be dimension-specific.

**5. The D1/D11 merger in yo and ta creates a constructional overlap not present in other languages.** In yo, the *tọ́* root covers both propositional correctness (D1: *ó tọ́*, "it is correct") and procedural/moral correctness (D11: *ó tọ́ pé*, "it is right that") without lexical differentiation. In ta, *cari* covers both factual correctness (D1) and procedural correctness (D11). In ka, fi, and ko, distinct vocabulary is used for these two functions. This merger means that in yo and ta, the constructional distinctions between D1 and D11 are not lexically encoded; context determines which dimension is operative.

**6. The D4/D7 partial merger in eu creates a constructional overlap not present in other languages.** In eu, *benetakoa* covers both "genuine (not fake)" (D4) and "sincere (not performed)" (D7), and *benetan* functions as both an authenticity marker and a sincerity marker. In fi and ko, more distinct vocabulary is used for these two functions. This merger means that in eu, some constructional distinctions between D4 and D7 are not lexically encoded.

**7. The three-way inchoative verb distinction in ko (*드러나다/밝혀지다/판명되다*) for D1 and D10 is unique in the dataset.** Korean documents three distinct inchoative verbs for truth-revelation with slightly different nuances: *드러나다* (exposed/surfaced, stronger sense of unwanted revelation), *밝혀지다* (revealed through investigation, more neutral), *판명되다* (officially determined, most formal). Other languages typically use a single inchoative verb for this function. The ko three-way distinction encodes nuances of agency, formality, and the nature of the revelation process that other languages express through context or additional modifiers.

**8. The *-hada/-doeda* stative/agentive distinction in ko is unique in the dataset.** Korean documents a systematic semantic distinction between *jinsil-hada* (to be truthful, active/performed quality) and *jinsil-doeda* (to be truthful, inherent/resultant quality). This morphological distinction between performed and inherent quality is not documented in any other language in the dataset. It affects CF1 (predicative attribution) and CF5 (causative) for D1, D2, D4, and D7 in ko.

## Confidence Assessment

### Strong Evidence

The following matrix cells are supported by explicit documentation in the F4 construction tables and F5 opposition tables of multiple languages, with consistent patterns across unrelated language families:

- **CF1 (Predicative Attribution) × all dimensions: ALLOWED** — Documented in all 8 languages for all 12 dimensions. No restrictions documented.
- **CF3 (Adnominal Modification) × all dimensions: ALLOWED** — Documented in all 8 languages for all 12 dimensions. The yo postnominal pattern is a structural variant, not a restriction.
- **CF6 (Abstract Nominalization) × all dimensions: ALLOWED** — Documented in all 8 languages for all 12 dimensions. Specific suffix varies but functional outcome is consistent.
- **CF7 (Agentive Nominalization) × all dimensions: BLOCKED for positive roles** — Explicitly documented as absent in all 8 languages for all dimensions. The most consistently documented blocked pathway in the dataset.
- **CF10 (Truth-Revelation / Concealment) × D1 and D10: ALLOWED** — Documented in all 8 languages for D1 and D10. The intransitive emergence construction is the most robust constructional pattern in the dataset.
- **CF12 (Proverbial / Fixed Moral Assertion) × D1: ALLOWED** — Documented in all 8 languages for D1. The proverbial assertion that truth ultimately prevails is consistent across all language families.
- **CF2 (Negative Attribution) × all dimensions: ALLOWED** — Documented in all 8 languages for all 12 dimensions. Specific negation strategy varies but functional outcome is consistent.

### Moderate Evidence

The following matrix cells are supported by documentation in 4–6 languages or by explicit documentation in fewer languages with consistent patterns:

- **CF4 (Inchoative / Change-of-State) × D1, D4, D5, D10: ALLOWED** — Documented in at least 5 languages for each of these dimensions.
- **CF5 (Causative) × D1, D4, D9, D10: ALLOWED** — Documented in at least 5 languages for each of these dimensions.
- **CF9 (Existential / Scalar Predication) × D3, D7, D9: ALLOWED** — Documented in at least 3 languages for each of these dimensions, with ko showing the most systematic use.
- **CF10 (Truth-Revelation / Concealment) × D5, D6, D9, D11: INSUFFICIENT DATA** — The absence of documentation for these dimensions is consistent across languages but may reflect gaps in data collection rather than a genuine prohibition.
- **CF8 (Discourse Framing) × D1: ALLOWED** — Documented in all 8 languages for D1, though the degree of grammaticalization varies considerably.
- **CF11 (Parallel Morphological Opposition) × D1: VARIABLE** — Documented as a productive pattern only in tr; partial parallels in fi and eu.
- **CF12 (Proverbial / Fixed Moral Assertion) × D6: INSUFFICIENT DATA** — The absence of proverbial constructions for D6 is consistent across all 8 languages but may reflect the technical nature of precision evaluation rather than a genuine prohibition.

### Weak or Missing Evidence

The following matrix cells are based on limited documentation or on the absence of documentation, which may reflect data gaps rather than genuine constraints:

- **CF4, CF5 × D2, D3, D6, D7, D8, D11, D12: VARIABLE** — These cells are rated VARIABLE based on partial documentation in 2–4 languages. The evidence is insufficient to determine whether the pattern is broadly available or restricted.
- **CF8 × D3, D4, D5, D9, D12: INSUFFICIENT DATA** — The absence of discourse-framing constructions for these dimensions is consistent across languages but may reflect the institutional/technical nature of these dimensions rather than a genuine prohibition.
- **CF9 × D1, D2, D4, D5, D6, D8, D11, D12: VARIABLE or INSUFFICIENT DATA** — The existential/scalar predication construction is documented for some dimensions in some languages but is not consistently documented across all languages for these dimensions.
- **CF11 × most dimensions: INSUFFICIENT DATA** — The parallel morphological opposition construction is documented as a productive pattern only in tr. The absence in other languages may reflect language-specific morphological properties rather than a cross-linguistic constraint.
- **CF7 × D3, D5, D6, D8, D9, D11: VARIABLE** — Agentive nominals for institutional roles (judge, witness, examiner) are attested in some languages for these dimensions, but these are institutional role nouns rather than agentive nominals derived from the relevant bases. The evidence is insufficient to determine whether the positive-role agentive blockage extends to these dimensions or is specific to D1, D2, D4, D7, and D12.

## Preliminary Notes

The empirical matrix (G7a) was derived inductively from F-phase cross-linguistic data across 8 languages. The AOML matrix is a theoretical model with 7 primary axes, 2 meta-axes, 7 core operators, 4 levels, and a set of structural rules. The comparison below maps empirical dimensions (D1–D12) and constructional functions (CF1–CF12) against AOML structures where mappings are supportable. Where no mapping is supportable, this is stated explicitly.

The empirical matrix uses 12 semantic dimensions and 12 constructional functions. AOML uses 7 primary axes, 7 operators, and 6 structural rules. The two systems are not isomorphic: the empirical system is finer-grained in some areas and coarser in others. Several empirical dimensions map to subregions within a single AOML axis; several AOML axes have no direct empirical dimension counterpart.

## Summary

### Confirmed Patterns

**1. ATTR is universally licensed across all primary axes (D1–D12 × CF1).**
Every empirical dimension shows ALLOWED for predicative attribution across all 8 languages. This is the strongest positive confirmation of AOML's licensing of ATTR as a universal operator.

**2. CONTR is universally licensed across all primary axes (D1–D12 × CF2).**
Negative attribution is universally available. AOML's licensing of CONTR is confirmed.

**3. ABSTR is universally licensed for VER, AUTH, SINC, NORM, VERIF (D1–D6, D9, D11 × CF6).**
Abstract nominalization is universally productive for these dimensions. AOML's licensing of ABSTR on these axes is confirmed.

**4. Rule R1 (CAUSE × SINC universally blocked) is strongly confirmed.**
The empirical data confirms that direct causation of dispositional character traits (honesty, sincerity, integrity) is blocked across all 8 languages. This is the strongest single empirical-AOML alignment in the dataset. The block is consistent across South Caucasian, Niger-Congo, Finno-Ugric, language isolate, Dravidian, Austronesian, Turkic, and Koreanic language families.

**5. Rule R3 (CAUSE(+) × AUTH blocked; CAUSE(−) × AUTH licensed) is confirmed.**
The empirical data confirms the polarity asymmetry for authenticity causation: "manufacture authentic goods" is blocked; "forge the document" is natural. This is a strong empirical-AOML alignment.

**6. Rule R4 (Positive emergence bias) is confirmed.**
The empirical data confirms that positive emergence (truth comes to light, claim turns out to be true) is natural and productive across all 8 languages, while negative emergence (truth becomes false) is marked or blocked. This asymmetry is consistent across language families.

**7. CF10 (Truth-Revelation / Concealment) × D1 and D10 is strongly confirmed.**
The intransitive truth-revelation construction (truth as grammatical subject of emergence verb) is documented in all 8 languages. This is the primary empirical evidence for REVEAL as a candidate primitive operator. The construction is consistent with AOML's provisional licensing of REVEAL on VER.

**8. ATTR × VERIF is confirmed (D9 × CF1, CF3, CF6).**
Evidence and proof vocabulary is universally available for predicative attribution, adnominal modification, and abstract nominalization. AOML's licensing of ATTR on VERIF is confirmed.

**9. CAUSE × VERIF is confirmed (D9 × CF5).**
Causative constructions for proving and verifying are attested across all 8 languages. AOML's licensing of CAUSE × VERIF under conditions is confirmed.

---

### Partial or Conditional Matches

**1. D3 (Source Trustworthiness vs. Content Credibility) maps onto two AOML axes (SINC and VER).**
The empirical source/content distinction is coherent within AOML but requires two axes rather than one. Source trustworthiness maps to SINC (reliability, faithfulness subregion); content credibility maps to VER. AOML does not model this as a single dimension but the two-axis mapping is internally consistent.

**2. D6 (Precision and Exactness) maps onto DEG[VER] in AOML.**
The empirical precision dimension is finer-grained than AOML's treatment. AOML handles precision as a DEG modulation of VER rather than as a primary axis. The scalar predication constructions (accuracy is high/low) are consistent with DEG[VER]. The empirical dimension is not lost but is subsumed under a meta-axis modulation.

**3. D7 (Authenticity of Inner States) maps onto SINC in AOML, but the causative conflict is partial.**
Rule R1 predicts that direct causation of inner-state authenticity is blocked. Empirical data shows CF5 is VARIABLE for D7 — some indirect facilitation constructions are attested. The conflict is partial: direct causation of the dispositional state is blocked, but indirect facilitation (creating conditions for authenticity) is attested. AOML's R1 may need to distinguish direct from indirect causation more explicitly.

**4. D8 (Appearance vs. Underlying Reality) maps onto STRAT in AOML.**
The appearance/reality contrast is consistent with STRAT — the operator marking internal contrast within an axis. AOML licenses STRAT on VER and AUTH. The empirical dimension is not lost but is subsumed under an operator rather than a primary axis.

**5. D11 (Correctness of Reasoning) maps onto VERIF and NORM in AOML.**
The empirical dimension conflates logical reasoning correctness (VERIF) and moral/practical judgment correctness (NORM). AOML does not model this as a single dimension but the two-axis mapping is coherent.

**6. D12 (Deliberate Deception vs. Innocent Error) requires two AOML axes (VER + SINC).**
The empirical distinction between deliberate deception and innocent error requires both the falsity of the claim (VER) and the deceptive intent of the agent (SINC). AOML does not model this as a single dimension but the two-axis mapping is coherent and consistent with R1.

**7. BECOME × NORM and BECOME × VERIF are restricted but not blocked.**
Empirical data shows inchoative constructions for validity/legitimacy and reasoning correctness are attested but less productive than for D1 or D4. AOML restricts BECOME on these axes. The empirical data is consistent with restriction rather than blocking.

**8. DEG as meta-axis modulation is partially confirmed.**
Scalar predication constructions (accuracy is high/low, credibility is high/low) are consistent with DEG modulating VER and SINC. However, the empirical data does not directly test the substitution prohibition (Rule R5). The prohibition is a constraint on inference, not on the availability of scalar constructions.

---

### Conflicts

**1. D7 (Authenticity of Inner States) × CF5 (Causative): partial conflict with Rule R1.**
Rule R1 predicts universal blocking of CAUSE × SINC. Empirical data shows some causative constructions for inner-state authenticity are attested (eu *zintzotu eragin*, ko *진정성을 높이다*). These constructions appear to cause conditions for authenticity rather than authenticity itself, but the boundary between direct and indirect causation is not clearly specified in AOML. This is a genuine tension that requires clarification.

**Severity assessment:** Moderate. The conflict is real but may be resolvable by distinguishing direct causation of the dispositional state from indirect facilitation of conditions for that state. AOML's R1 as stated ("direct causation of dispositional character traits is structurally prohibited") may be too broad if it blocks indirect facilitation constructions that are empirically attested.

---

### Unmodeled Empirical Findings

**1. The positive agentive nominalization block (CF7 positive role) is not predicted by AOML.**
The most consistently documented empirical finding in the dataset — that no language has a lexicalized single-word agentive for a habitual truth-teller, honest person (as a role noun), or authenticator — is not predicted or explained by AOML. AOML does not model agentive nominalization as a distinct operator. The asymmetry between negative agentive availability (liar, forger, deceiver: ALLOWED in all 8 languages) and positive agentive unavailability (truth-teller, honest person: BLOCKED in all 8 languages) is a robust cross-linguistic finding that falls outside AOML's current architecture.

**2. Discourse framing constructions (CF8) are not modeled by AOML.**
The grammaticalized or semi-grammaticalized discourse markers for frank disclosure and correction of prior assumptions (id *sebenarnya*, tr *aslında*, ta *uṇmaiyil*, ka *simartle rom vtq̇vat*) are not captured by any AOML operator. These constructions function at the pragmatic-discourse level rather than the semantic-structural level that AOML models.

**3. Proverbial / fixed moral assertion constructions (CF12) are not modeled by AOML.**
The cross-linguistic proverbial pattern asserting the ultimate triumph or indestructibility of truth (yo *òtítọ́ kò ní kú*, ta *uṇmai tāṉ vellum*, ko *진실은 하나다*) is not captured by any AOML operator. These constructions function at the pragmatic-cultural level.

**4. The neutral-copy / fraudulent-fake three-way distinction within D4 is not modeled by AOML.**
The empirical data documents a consistent three-way distinction in at least 6 languages: original/genuine (AUTH positive), neutral copy/imitation (AUTH neutral intermediate), and fraudulent fake (AUTH negative, CAUSE(−) applied). AOML models AUTH as a binary (genuine vs. counterfeit) without a neutral intermediate position. The neutral intermediate (imitation without fraudulent intent) is a stable cross-linguistic category that falls outside AOML's current AUTH modeling.

**5. The D1/D11 merger in Yoruba and Tamil is not predicted by AOML.**
In yo and ta, the same root covers both propositional correctness (D1) and procedural/moral correctness (D11) without lexical differentiation. AOML treats VER and NORM as distinct axes. The empirical merger in two unrelated language families suggests that the VER/NORM boundary may be less stable cross-linguistically than AOML assumes.

**6. The Korean *있다/없다* existential frame as the primary predication strategy for *-seong* nominals is not predicted by AOML.**
The morphological restriction in Korean that blocks *-hada* predicative suffixation on *-seong* quality nominals, forcing the existential *있다/없다* frame, is a language-specific constructional constraint not modeled by AOML. AOML does not model morphological restrictions on predication strategies.

**7. The three-way inchoative verb distinction in Korean (*드러나다/밝혀지다/판명되다*) is not predicted by AOML.**
Korean documents three distinct inchoative verbs for truth-revelation with different nuances of agency, formality, and the nature of the revelation process. AOML models REVEAL as a single provisional operator without internal differentiation.

**8. The parallel morphological opposition pattern (CF11) in Turkish is not predicted by AOML.**
The tr *doğrulamak/yanlışlamak* productive morphological pair encoding the verify/falsify distinction, with parallel *doğrulanabilirlik/yanlışlanabilirlik* nominalizations, is a language-specific elaboration not predicted by AOML.

---

### Unattested AOML Structures

**1. AOML LIFE axis is not directly tested by the empirical data.**
The empirical data does not include a lifelikeness or verisimilitude dimension as a distinct semantic category. D6 (Precision and Exactness) partially overlaps with LIFE but is more naturally mapped to DEG[VER]. The LIFE axis's key diagnostic — that ABSTR × LIFE is blocked and REVEAL × LIFE is blocked — cannot be evaluated from the available data.

**2. AOML Rule R2 (CAUSE × ESS blocked; BECOME × ESS blocked) is not directly tested.**
D8 (Appearance vs. Underlying Reality) partially maps to ESS but the empirical data does not directly test CAUSE × ESS or BECOME × ESS as distinct constructions. The empirical data is consistent with R2 but does not provide direct confirmation.

**3. AOML Rule R6 (TEMP meta-axis) is not tested.**
The empirical data does not include temporal constructions as a distinct dimension. The TEMP meta-axis is provisional in AOML and is not evaluated by the available empirical data.

**4. AOML REVEAL provisional operator: the LIFE-blocks-REVEAL diagnostic is not testable.**
The key diagnostic for REVEAL as a primitive — that LIFE blocks REVEAL while other axes license it — cannot be evaluated because the empirical data does not include a LIFE dimension.

**5. AOML ESS axis is only partially tested.**
D8 (Appearance vs. Underlying Reality) partially maps to ESS, but the empirical data does not provide a direct test of ESS-specific operator licensing. The ESS axis's distinctive predictions (CAUSE blocked, BECOME blocked, RESULT restricted) are not directly confirmed or disconfirmed by the available data.

---

## Theoretical Discussion

### Where AOML Appears Strongly Supported

**Rule R1 (Dispositional Causation Block) receives the strongest empirical support in the dataset.** The universal blocking of direct causation of dispositional character traits (honesty, sincerity, integrity) across all 8 languages and all language families is the most robust single finding. The empirical data independently confirms AOML's strongest structural rule. This alignment is particularly significant because it was derived from 16 languages in AOML and is confirmed here by 8 additional languages using a different data collection methodology.

**Rule R3 (Authenticity Polarity Asymmetry) receives strong empirical support.** The blocking of CAUSE(+) × AUTH and the licensing of CAUSE(−) × AUTH is confirmed by the empirical data. The three-way distinction between original/genuine, neutral copy, and fraudulent fake (documented in at least 6 languages) is consistent with AOML's treatment of AUTH as an ontological target type where positive causation is blocked but negative causation (forgery, destruction of authenticity) is licensed.

**Rule R4 (Positive Emergence Bias) receives strong empirical support.** The universal preference for positive emergence constructions (truth comes to light, claim turns out to be true) over negative emergence constructions (truth becomes false) is confirmed across all 8 languages. The intransitive truth-revelation construction (CF10) is the canonical realization of this bias.

**The REVEAL provisional operator receives strong indirect support.** The intransitive truth-revelation construction is documented in all 8 languages across unrelated language families. The construction presupposes a latent pre-existing state that was already true before disclosure — precisely the presupposition that distinguishes REVEAL from RESULT + STRAT. The empirical data supports AOML's provisional licensing of REVEAL on VER and its identification as a candidate primitive.

**The target-type ontology receives indirect support.** The empirical data is consistent with AOML's three-way target-type classification (FACTUAL, EPISTEMIC, DISPOSITIONAL). The differential operator licensing across these types — CAUSE licensed for factual targets, blocked for dispositional targets, restricted for epistemic targets — is confirmed by the empirical data.

### Where AOML May Require Refinement

**1. Rule R1 may need to distinguish direct from indirect causation more explicitly.**
The empirical data shows that while direct causation of dispositional character traits is universally blocked, indirect facilitation constructions (creating conditions for honesty, encouraging authenticity) are attested in some languages. AOML's R1 as stated ("direct causation of dispositional character traits is structurally prohibited") is consistent with this distinction but does not make it explicit. A refinement would specify that R1 blocks CAUSE applied directly to the dispositional state but does not block CAUSE applied to conditions that may facilitate the dispositional state.

**2. The AUTH axis may need a neutral intermediate position.**
The empirical data documents a consistent three-way distinction in at least 6 languages: original/genuine (AUTH positive), neutral copy/imitation (AUTH neutral intermediate), and fraudulent fake (AUTH negative). AOML models AUTH as a binary (genuine vs. counterfeit) without a neutral intermediate. The neutral intermediate — imitation without fraudulent intent — is a stable cross-linguistic category. A refinement would add a neutral intermediate position to the AUTH axis, distinguishing CAUSE(−) applied with fraudulent intent from CAUSE(−) applied without fraudulent intent.

**3. The VER/NORM boundary may be less stable cross-linguistically than AOML assumes.**
The empirical D1/D11 merger in Yoruba and Tamil — where the same root covers both propositional correctness (VER) and procedural/moral correctness (NORM) — suggests that the VER/NORM boundary is not universally maintained. AOML treats VER and NORM as distinct axes with different default methods and validation habitats. The empirical merger in two unrelated language families suggests that the boundary may be a gradient rather than a sharp distinction in some languages.

**4. The agentive nominalization asymmetry requires modeling.**
The most consistently documented empirical finding — the universal blocking of positive agentive nominals for truth-tellers, honest persons, and authenticators — is not predicted by AOML. This asymmetry is consistent across all 8 languages and all language families. A refinement would add a constraint to the operator system specifying that ABSTR applied to the positive pole of SINC and VER in agentive nominalization contexts is blocked or strongly dispreferred. The constraint may be related to the dispositional causation block (R1): if dispositional character traits cannot be externally caused, they may also resist being named as stable role identities.

**5. The discourse-framing and proverbial construction types require acknowledgment.**
AOML does not model discourse-level framing constructions (CF8) or proverbial/fixed moral assertion constructions (CF12). These are pragmatic-level phenomena that fall outside AOML's current semantic-structural scope. A refinement would acknowledge these as pragmatic projections of the semantic structure rather than as gaps in the model. The discourse-framing constructions (sebenarnya, aslında, uṇmaiyil) are grammaticalized realizations of STRAT × VER — the contrast between surface appearance and underlying reality. The proverbial constructions are culturally fixed realizations of RESULT × VER with a temporal dimension (truth will eventually prevail).

### Where Empirical Findings Suggest New Dimensions, Constructional Constraints, or Revised Constraint Strength

**1. The positive agentive nominalization block may be a new structural rule.**
The universal blocking of positive agentive nominals for truth-tellers and honest persons across all 8 languages and all language families is a robust empirical finding that AOML does not currently model. This finding suggests a new structural rule: **ABSTR(agentive) × SINC(positive pole) → blocked; ABSTR(agentive) × VER(positive pole) → blocked**. The rule would explain why "truth-teller" and "honest person" (as role nouns) are universally absent while "liar" and "forger" are universally present. The rule may be derivable from R1 (if dispositional character traits cannot be externally caused, they resist being named as stable role identities) or may be an independent constraint.

**2. The neutral-copy intermediate in AUTH may require a new subregion or axis-internal distinction.**
The consistent three-way distinction (original/neutral copy/fraudulent fake) in at least 6 languages suggests that AUTH has an internal structure that AOML does not currently model. The neutral intermediate is not simply a weaker version of the fraudulent fake — it has different operator licensing (CAUSE(−) without fraudulent intent is licensed; CAUSE(−) with fraudulent intent is the canonical AUTH violation). A new subregion within AUTH — distinguishing CAUSE(−) with intent from CAUSE(−) without intent — would capture this distinction.

**3. The D1/D11 merger in Yoruba and Tamil suggests that VER and NORM may share a common root in some languages.**
The empirical merger of propositional correctness (VER) and procedural/moral correctness (NORM) in two unrelated language families suggests that the VER/NORM distinction may be a secondary elaboration rather than a primitive distinction. AOML treats VER and NORM as distinct primary axes. The empirical data suggests that some languages treat them as subregions of a single correctness axis. This does not necessarily require revising AOML's axis structure, but it suggests that the VER/NORM boundary should be treated as a gradient rather than a sharp distinction.

**4. The REVEAL operator's empirical support is strong enough to warrant elevation from provisional to confirmed status, pending cross-architectural validation.**
The intransitive truth-revelation construction is documented in all 8 languages across unrelated language families. The construction's presupposition of a latent pre-existing state is consistent across languages. The empirical data provides strong support for REVEAL as a primitive operator. The remaining obstacle to confirmation — cross-architectural validation using non-Claude LLM families — is a methodological constraint rather than an empirical one. The current empirical data is consistent with REVEAL being a genuine primitive.

**5. The discourse-framing constructions (CF8) may be a pragmatic projection of STRAT × VER.**
The grammaticalized discourse markers for frank disclosure and correction of prior assumptions (sebenarnya, aslında, uṇmaiyil) signal a contrast between surface appearance and underlying reality. This is consistent with STRAT × VER — the operator marking internal contrast within the VER axis. The grammaticalization of these constructions across unrelated language families suggests that STRAT × VER has a strong pragmatic projection into discourse-level framing. AOML could acknowledge this projection without adding a new operator.

**6. The proverbial constructions (CF12) may be a pragmatic projection of RESULT × VER with TEMP modulation.**
The cross-linguistic proverbial pattern asserting the ultimate triumph of truth (truth will not die, truth always comes to the surface) is consistent with RESULT × VER modulated by TEMP (temporal persistence). The proverbial constructions assert that the RESULT state (truth established) is temporally persistent and inevitable. AOML could acknowledge this as a pragmatic projection of RESULT × VER + TEMP[VER] without adding a new operator.

### CU-1. Predicative attribution is universally available for truth-domain properties

**Statement.** In all eight languages, a subject can receive a truth-domain predicate (true, false, genuine, accurate, valid, honest, credible) through a copular or stative construction. No language restricts this function to a subset of truth-domain dimensions.

**Evidence summary.** CF1 (Predicative Attribution) is rated ALLOWED across all twelve semantic dimensions in all eight languages (ka, yo, fi, eu, ta, id, tr, ko). The specific copular form varies — enclitic *-a* in Georgian, zero copula in Tamil/Indonesian/Turkish/Korean, overt copula in Finnish/Basque/Yoruba — but the constructional function is universally available. No documented restriction on predicate type or dimension was found.

**Caveats / exceptions.** The Korean *있다/없다* existential frame substitutes for standard copular predication for *-seong* quality nominals (D3, D7, D9, D11), but this is a morphological restriction on a specific suffix class, not a restriction on the predicative attribution function itself. The function remains available; only the surface realization differs.

**Confidence rating.** High.

---

### CU-2. Adnominal modification is universally available for truth-domain evaluative terms

**Statement.** In all eight languages, truth-domain evaluative terms can modify nouns in attributive position (accurate information, forged document, reliable source, honest person). No language restricts this function to a subset of truth-domain dimensions.

**Evidence summary.** CF3 (Adnominal Modification) is rated ALLOWED across all twelve semantic dimensions in all eight languages. The modifier position varies — prenominal in seven languages, postnominal in Yoruba — but the constructional function is universally available.

**Caveats / exceptions.** The Yoruba postnominal pattern is a systematic structural difference in modifier position, not a restriction on the function. Indonesian restricts direct juxtaposition (without the *yang* relativizer) to fixed collocations, but the *yang* relativizer construction is fully productive and unrestricted.

**Confidence rating.** High.

---

### CU-3. Abstract nominalization of truth-domain properties is universally productive

**Statement.** In all eight languages, truth-domain properties (truthfulness, accuracy, credibility, validity, honesty, authenticity) can be named as abstract entities through a productive morphological process. The resulting nominals serve as subjects, objects, and genitive modifiers.

**Evidence summary.** CF6 (Abstract Nominalization) is rated ALLOWED across all twelve semantic dimensions in all eight languages. Specific suffixes vary: *-eba/-oba* (Georgian), *ì-* prefix (Yoruba), *-uus/-yys* (Finnish), *-tasun* (Basque), *-mai* (Tamil), *ke-...-an* circumfix (Indonesian), *-luk/-lik* (Turkish), *-seong* (Korean). The functional outcome is consistent across all languages and all dimensions.

**Caveats / exceptions.** The degree of elaboration varies: Korean *-seong* nominals are more systematically documented than Tamil *-mai* compounds for some dimensions. Some abstract nominals are restricted to formal registers (Georgian *egiazkotasun*, Finnish *totuudellinen*). These are register restrictions, not restrictions on the availability of the nominalization function.

**Confidence rating.** High.

### CU-4. Negative attribution is universally available for truth-domain properties

**Statement.** In all eight languages, truth-domain predicates can be negated. The negation may be syntactic (negation particle + copula) or morphological (privative prefix/circumfix), but the function is universally available.

**Evidence summary.** CF2 (Negative Attribution) is rated ALLOWED across all twelve semantic dimensions in all eight languages. Syntactic negation is universal; morphological privative negation is additionally documented in at least six languages (Georgian *u-...-o*, Finnish *epä-*, Basque *ez-/-gabe*, Tamil *-aṟṟa*, Indonesian *ke-tidak-...-an*, Turkish *-sız*, Korean *부-*).

**Caveats / exceptions.** The specific negation strategy varies and is not always interchangeable within a language. Indonesian distinguishes *tidak* (adjectival predicates) from *bukan* (nominal predicates); Korean distinguishes *아니다* (nominal) from *-지 않다* (adjectival). **Confidence rating.** High.
